site.title: Computational Biophysicist | Molecular Modeling & Scientific Computing
site.description: Sikao Guo develops validated computational methods and reusable C++/Python software for protein conformational sampling, biomolecular self-assembly, structural bioinformatics, and high-performance simulation.
site.availability: Open to U.S.-based Research Scientist and Research Software Engineer roles

impactStats.label: One specification to VMD, PyMOL, and web

highlights: Developed a cross-platform GUI code-generation framework that automated interface generation for 9 computational biology applications across VMD, PyMOL, and web platforms.
Engineered a C++ protein backbone sampler that generalized inverse-kinematics loop sampling to backbone and intrinsically disordered region conformational sampling using SE(3)-based rigid-body moves.
Built an automated structural validation pipeline integrating AttnPacker, OpenMM, and PhiSiCal for reproducible evaluation and benchmarking of sampled protein conformations.

Parallelized the C++ NERDSS reaction-diffusion simulator using MPI domain decomposition, achieving approximately 90x acceleration on 96 CPUs for a 20,000-particle benchmark while preserving serial kinetics and diffusion.

Developed structure-resolved computational models of clathrin-mediated endocytosis and HIV-1 assembly, revealing mechanisms governing critical nucleus formation, adaptor stoichiometry, and Gag-Pol dimerization.

Developed ioNERDSS, a Python toolkit that automates conversion of PDB/mmCIF structures into simulation-ready coarse-grained reaction-diffusion models and was benchmarked across more than 44,000 PDB structures.
Implemented computational-geometry methods for interface detection and reaction-network generation, and integrated machine-learned predictors for binding-affinity initialization.
